text:
alex_sales: Hey team — putting together the POC network handoff for Zentri Health. They want Redwood Private (VPC) access for the eval. Two asks from customer: (1) Private connectivity via PrivateLink preferred, fallback to VPC peering. (2) A short checklist of what they must provision (subnets, route tables, SGs) and what we provide (VPCE ID, service name, hosted API key vs dedicated pool IPs).

Tess_SE: Thanks Alex. We should confirm the customer CIDR and whether they need cross-account interface endpoint. Quick checklist from our side: we provide the endpoint service name (com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-xxx) and the VPCE acceptance flow if private. For Dedicated pools we also provide the allowed egress IPs for the pool.

Tess_SE: Minimal customer requirements to provision (paste this to customer):
```
- One private subnet in each AZ you want low-latency in (eg eu-west-1a/b)
- Route table entry: route to our VPCE (if peering, route to peer CIDR via peer attachment)
- Security group allowing outbound TLS to our endpoint on 443
- Optional: NAT/GW if you expect outbound internet from private subnets
- On-prem firewall: allow <our endpoint IPs> / service hostname
```

Tess_SE: For PrivateLink (preferred): we need their VPCE id and security group they attach to the endpoint. For VPC peering we need the peer VPC ID, exact CIDR block, and the route table IDs to update.

Dan_Infra: A few infra notes:
- If they're on TGW, ensure attachment propagation for the route table is configured and that we don't rely on route propagation for VPCEs (use explicit routes).
- Subnet sizes: /24 per AZ is fine for POC. Avoid overlapping with our side.
- If using peering, remember peering doesn't support transitive routing; cross-account peering across multiple VPCs requires explicit routes.

Kyle_Network: On PrivateLink specifics: we expose an interface endpoint. We'll provide the endpoint service name: `com.redwood-inference.service.vpce` (placeholder until we create the service in their region). Customer should set up an interface endpoint with a security group that allows outbound HTTPS. Example CLI to create endpoint (customer):
```
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \ 
  --vpc-id vpc-0abcd1234 \ 
  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \ 
  --service-name com.redwood-inference.service.vpce.us-west-2 \ 
  --subnet-ids subnet-0a1b2c3d subnet-0e4f5g6h \ 
  --security-group-ids sg-0123456789abcdef0
```

Kyle_Network: For Dedicated pool customers: we can provide a set of static egress IPs that you must allow in your SGs/firewall. If they want requests to appear from their VPC (no egress), we need a different setup (private deployment).

Sarah_Acme: Quick clarifying Q from Zentri: they will be using 10.50.0.0/16 for the POC VPC. They asked: "Does PrivateLink support cross-account? We don't want to hand over route table edits to multiple teams." Also they asked whether we can accept a VPC endpoint in non-prod only and provide a hosted API key for initial tests.

Tess_SE: PrivateLink supports cross-account interface endpoints. The owner of the endpoint can request acceptance if the service requires manual acceptance. For the POC we can set the service to require acceptance and have us accept after they create the endpoint. Hosted API key is fine for quick validation but for a Private deployment test we typically do:
- Hosted API key for smoke tests (we issue a scoped API key tied to the POC project)
- Configure PrivateLink/VPCE for secure traffic
- If they want Dedicated pool routing, we'll share egress IP list (or whitelist our subnet ranges if using peering)

Tess_SE: If they prefer peering instead of PrivateLink, ask them to provide: peer VPC ID, owner account ID, CIDR block, and one route table per AZ to update. Also confirm if they require IAM or resource-based policy on the endpoint.

Dan_Infra: FYI on acceptance: once they create the VPCE we will see a pending acceptance. We will accept, then they should verify DNS (private DNS or explicit hostnames). For PrivateLink ensure they disable private DNS if they want to resolve service hostnames differently.

Kyle_Network: Routing snippet to share with their networking team (if using peering):
```
# add route to our peer CIDR
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc1234 --destination-cidr-block 172.31.200.0/22 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0a1b2c3d
```

Infra-bot: Incident ticket INC-4578 created for Zentri POC network onboarding. Assignee: tess_se. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4578 :white_check_mark:

Alex_Sales: Customer also asked about compliance: they need audit logs of accepted VPCE connections and we need to confirm KMS usage for any data plane keys. Can infra confirm what logs we capture by default for PrivateLink?

Dan_Infra: We capture acceptance events and log them to the customer's audit trail in the private control plane (we can also export CloudTrail events to their S3 if requested). For KMS: if they request customer-managed keys for any hosted artifacts, we can integrate with their KMS in Private deployments, but for hosted PrivateLink traffic TLS is sufficient — no extra KMS needed for TLS.

Sarah_Acme: Ok sending VPCE request this afternoon. They want the exact service name and whether our team will accept within 4 hours of creation. Also asked if we can provide a temp hosted API key for dev-only traffic that expires in 7 days.

Tess_SE: We'll provide the service name once we create it in the target region. We'll accept the endpoint within the day (aim <4 hours) and can issue a 7-day scoped hosted API key for dev tests. Next steps for us:
- Create service in their region and share service name
- Provide dedicated pool egress IPs if they choose that route
- Wait for VPCE creation, accept, and confirm DNS & SG settings

Alex_Sales: Great — I'll schedule a 30m handoff call with Zentri networking and engineering for tomorrow 10am PT. I'll drop the calendar invite and include this checklist. Thanks all :thumbsup:
